STATEMENT OF OBJECTIVES The objective and technical scope of this proposed project is to develop and apply the MMN multiscale finite element framework to predict the bending performance of high strength automotive aluminum sheet alloys and guide the design of its optimum process conditions for best SPR rivet-ability for vehicle light weighting. This will start with the acquisition of an AA6111 alloy with T6 temper condition. After microstructural characterization in both mesoscale and nanoscale and bending performance characterization at Ford, the MMN framework will be applied to this alloy to simulate 3-point bending. Starting from macro-model of 3-point bending, the critical region of fracture will be identified, and the region geometry will be used to construct the micro-model. The fracture criterion of micron-scale precipitates and ALNP matrix in the micro-model will be calibrated and validated by comparing simulated and measured bending results. With the ALNP fracture strain obtained, the fracture strain of Al- matrix in ALNP will similarly be determined by the nano-model using an edge-constrained FE modeling approach (Fig. 2) developed by Hu et al. [5], [6]. 4 After the MMN framework is built and fracture criterion calibrated, massive number of nano- model FE simulations will be performed to obtain a reduced order surrogate model (ROSM) of the fracture criterion of the ALNP as a function of volume fraction, size, and distribution of the nanoparticle and PFZ. This nano → micro modeling part allows exploration of the influence of different material nanostructures from different process conditions on the bending properties within the multiscale bending simulation framework. Further experimental validations will be done to verify the simulated bending performance of the material with different process conditions. 3. BENEFITS TO THE FUNDING DOE OFFICE’S MISSION The project will ensure accurate prediction of the microstructure effects on bendability and rivetability of high strength automotive Al sheet alloys, giving guidance to the process optimization of the alloy process to reach the department of energy goal considerable vehicle light-weighting and cost-cutting and promote the EV adoption and substantial decarbonization. 4. TECHNICAL DISCUSSION OF THE WORK PERFORMED BY ALL PARTIES In order to most effectively and efficiently meet the project objectives outlined above, the team established a plan as follows: 1) Alloy acquisition and characterization 2) Apply the macro→micro scheme to calibrate the fracture criterion of the matrix materials 3) Nano-model development and calibration 4) Parametric studies using nano-model and reduced order model development of ALNP fracture strain as a function of nano-precipitates distributions. 5) Microstructure characterization, mechanical testing of AA6111 alloys with several tempering conditions, and the application of the ROSM in the bendability prediction 4.1 Alloy acquisition and characterization 4.1.1 Alloy acquisition Ford has acquired a high strength AA6111 alloy with T6 temper: 6HS2-T6.
